title: Time Stop Hero
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kuzuno Sekai, shunned after an embarrassing photo of him is posted online, wishes himself out of the world and wakes in a game-like fantasy world holding a controller whose pause button freezes time. He uses the frozen time both for perverted pranks (stripping and skirt-flipping) and to solve problems and defeat enemies, racing a hidden countdown that resets only when he performs heroic deeds (Wikipedia, Seven Seas).
life_message: A disgraced outcast can become a hero by using his power to save people, even while indulging himself along the way.

content.note: Battles with monsters and the Forces of Darkness (Wikipedia); MU lists Massacre and Sexual Violence with few votes (to verify).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Sekai answers his own humiliation by escaping, not by a duel of honor (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Freezing time puts him outside every rule of the world (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Small adventuring party with Niña and Fury (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Earns the title Hero of Salvation; rank secondary.

folkways.japan: Built on Japanese isekai and game conventions (status screens, stage clears) and on the ecchi-comedy tradition of the lecherous hero in shonen magazines.

delivery.evidence: Sources describe gags and problem-solving, not speeches; message carried by the timer resetting after heroic deeds (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The story offers little argument for or against its hero's conduct; it is played as comedy (to verify).

winners_losers: Sekai wins fights and gains companions while his pranks go largely unpunished; the Forces of Darkness lose. Sympathy rests with the self-indulgent but helpful hero.
